newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin proposes joint G7 force for Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin proposes joint G7 force for Peru crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday called on the countries of the Group of Seven rich nations to join efforts in helping resolve the hostage crisis in Peru, the Kremlin press service said.

Yeltsin's message to the G7 leaders said the assitance could include "possible dispatch there of special anti-terrorist squads from national security services". The proposal included Russia as well as the G7 members.

Yeltsin suggested that a joint declaration of the Group of Eight (the G7 plus Russia) should offer Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori "coordinated assistance in resolving the conflict including possible dispatch there of special anti-terrorist squads from national security services".
If Fujimori agreed, special services of the eight countries should set up a joint headquarters "with the aim of launching an operation to free the hostages".

"The situation in Lima requires that we should show in practice how we are able to act in order to help defenceless people who have become victims of terrorists," said a separate letter Yeltsin sent to Fujimori.
The letter said Russia was ready to send its own anti-terrorist group to Lima.
